findings.issue_text: The `if: :email_changed?` condition in `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true, email: true, if: :email_changed?` (app/models/user.rb:47) applies to every validator in the single validates call, silently disabling presence and uniqueness validation; for a new record with an unassigned email, `email_changed?` is false so all three email validations are skipped, letting `User.new(username: "x").valid?` return true and allowing a POST to /users without email to either persist a user with NULL email or hit a DB constraint violation swallowed by `rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` with a misleading 'something already taken' message

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb:10-13) performs DB writes as a side effect of model validation (increments match_count, updates last_match_at, and saves) when invoked from EmailValidator, so every `user.valid?` or `user.save` with a changed email executes a SELECT plus UPDATE against blocked_emails regardless of whether registration happens, polluting read-only validity checks (pre-checks, admin previews, background jobs, tests) and making the counters measure validation passes instead of registration attempts; counting should happen in the controller on failed create

The `match_count` increment in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-12) is a non-atomic read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`), so two concurrent requests with the same blocked email both read N and both persist N+1, losing updates; additionally the save's return value is ignored so failed stats writes are silently swallowed with no signal

The client pushes any rejected email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` exists (create_account_controller.js:274-276), which includes uniqueness ('has already been taken') and domain-whitelist errors, not just the new blocked case; `emailValidation` then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message, misidentifying the problem and discarding the server error reason so users with already-registered or domain-blocked emails cannot self-diagnose (e.g., realize they should log in instead)

`rejectedEmails` is never cleared (create_account_controller.js:17, 271-280) — it's defined on the controller class prototype (`Em.A([])`, shared across instances) and no code removes entries when the modal closes or a new attempt begins, so stale rejections persist for the entire page session with no invalidation path short of page reload; if the server-side reason for rejection changes mid-session (admin removes block, taken account deleted), the client still locally blocks an email the server would now accept

The blocked-email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb:10, `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`) is exact-match with no normalization — no downcasing or trimming on either the stored record or tested value — so on a case-sensitive database like Postgres a block stored as `spam@x.com` is bypassed by registering `SPAM@x.com`, and it only works on MySQL's default collation by accident, making the blocklist behavior silently differ by database backend

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18-21 (email_in_restriction_setting?, relocated from user.rb by this PR): the domain restriction check builds an unanchored regex (Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)) that matches @gmail.com anywhere in the string, and neither this validator nor the model (validates :email, email: true) performs any actual email format/RFC check, so with email_domains_whitelist set, addresses like attacker@gmail.com.evil.com or x@gmail.com@evil.com contain the substring @gmail.com and pass the whitelist while mail actually routes to the attacker-controlled gmail.com.evil.com domain; the blacklist direction has the inverse over-blocking bug, making the authz-adjacent signup restriction fully bypassable.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 (where(email: email), used from lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13): the blocked-email check is an exact, case-sensitive-on-PostgreSQL string match with no normalization (downcase/strip) and no plus-address handling, so a blocked abuser at bad@spamclub.com can re-register as Bad@spamclub.com, bad+1@spamclub.com, bad@spamclub.com. or ' bad@spamclub.com' — none match the stored row and all still deliver to the blocked mailbox on common providers, making the new control trivially evadable by exactly the motivated evaders it targets.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1 then save) with no atomic update_all/lock, so concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email lose increments; it also runs side-effectful DB writes inside validation on every valid?/save pass (double-counting when a controller flow validates twice), and record.save failures are silently ignored, making the match_count/last_match_at abuse metrics unreliable.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-276: any server response with errors.email — including 'has already been taken' or whitelist rejections — pushes values.email into rejectedEmails, after which the UI (line ~68) permanently reports 'is not allowed' for that address even if the real error was unrelated to validity, until page reload; this is client-side only (the server still enforces), but it misrepresents server errors and can wedge the form.

Blocked-email check in app/models/blocked_email.rb:11 (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`) is a byte-exact match on the raw submitted string, so on PostgreSQL (case-sensitive comparison) an admin-blocked `spammer@foo.com` is trivially bypassed by submitting `Spammer@foo.com` or `SPAMMER@foo.com`, while on MySQL (utf8_general_ci) case variants do match — enforcement silently differs depending on the deployment's database.

Due to the same non-normalization, the server echoes the stored `values.email` back to the client, which compares it to the user-typed `accountEmail` via `contains()`; any case/whitespace divergence makes the new `rejectedEmails` cache a silent no-op.

The create-account client (create_account_controller.js:274-276 and :68-72) discards the structured per-attribute error payload and uses it purely as a boolean: every email error — including 'already taken' and domain restrictions — is cached in `rejectedEmails` and rendered as the generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` ('is invalid'), so the specific server messages (e.g., the new `user.email.blocked` 'is not allowed.') never reach the field the user is looking at, producing contradictory flash vs. field messages.

`rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js:17) lives on the container-managed singleton modal controller and is never cleared — no reset on modal open or on successful submit — so an address rejected once (e.g., taken or blocked) keeps rendering as 'invalid' in fresh modal attempts for the whole page session until a full page reload, wrongly gating signup attempts after conditions may have changed.

`match_count` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:12-14 is incremented with a Ruby-side read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) instead of an atomic SQL `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1`, so concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address lose increments and the admin-facing `match_count`/`last_match_at` stats are understated.

The counter update is a committed DB write performed as a side effect of validation (invoked from lib/validators/email_validator.rb:17-19), so `user.valid?` alone mutates data — surprising for any caller using validity checks for inspection and breaking the expectation that `valid?` is read-only — and it can double-count when a record is validated more than once per request flow.

Non-atomic read-modify-write in BlockedEmail.should_block? (app/models/blocked_email.rb:12-17): the `match_count += 1` pattern has no locking or atomic SQL increment, so concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email race and lose increments; it should use an atomic update_all/increment_counter-style update.

In BlockedEmail.should_block?, the return value of `record.save` is ignored with no error handling, so a failed stats write is silently dropped — undercounting degrades the observability of which blocked emails are being hit (match_count/last_match_at are the documented operational signal), though the block/no-block decision itself stays correct.

EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13) performs a database write during validation by calling BlockedEmail.should_block?, so every user.valid?/save with a changed email executes a SELECT plus an UPDATE on blocked_emails as a side effect: validation is non-idempotent (repeated validations inflate match_count and last_match_at, so stats stop meaning attempts), stats-write exceptions now fail user creation (swallowed into a misleading generic 'login errors' message by the rescue in UsersController#create, while omniauth/admin creation flows would 500), and a row lock on the blocked record serializes concurrent signups on the hot path — blocking enforcement belongs in the save path, not inside validate_each.

The client-side rejectedEmails cache in create_account_controller.js is never cleared — not on success, not on modal close — and since Discourse controllers are long-lived singletons it persists for the whole SPA session, so a user whose email failed for a transient or resolvable reason (e.g., uniqueness race, an account that later gets renamed/deleted) can never retry that address from the page; it stays shown as user.email.invalid until a full reload.

rejectedEmails is over-broadly populated (create_account_controller.js:274-276): any server-side errors.email — including 'has already been taken' (uniqueness) and transient race outcomes — is pushed into the cache, so the message shown ('user.email.invalid') is wrong for 'already taken' errors and the inline reason diverges from the server's actual error.

No case/whitespace normalization on blocklist matching: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) (app/models/blocked_email.rb:12) and the client-side rejectedEmails.contains(email) (create_account_controller.js:70) are raw exact string comparisons with no downcase/strip, so a manually seeded entry stored as 'Evil@Spam.com' silently fails to block a user registering 'evil@spam.com' (and the client cache misses retyped variants) — strictly more brittle than the case-insensitive regex this code replaces.

Migration 20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb declares action_type null: false with no DB default while the default is only set via a before_validation model callback, so the documented workflow of bulk-loading blocked_emails rows directly via SQL (bypassing model callbacks) hits the NOT NULL constraint and fails with StatementInvalid; match_count got a DB default, action_type should too.

The new 'comprehensive' EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:3-12) still performs no basic format validation — validate_each only checks domain whitelist/blacklist plus the blocklist — so inputs like 'not-an-email' or 'abc' pass server-side whenever no domain restrictions are configured; server-side signup validation rests entirely on the client-side format check, meaning non-browser signup paths (API consumers, future endpoints) accept malformed addresses (a pre-existing gap carried over from user.rb#email_validator, not a regression).

No end-to-end test that a blocked email actually prevents registration — the PR's core feature (BlockedEmail model → EmailValidator wired into User via `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` → UsersController#create with the new errors/values fields → client handling) has zero integration coverage, so the suite stays green if any link in the chain breaks and the anti-spam feature would silently stop working.
The only EmailValidator spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` in both examples, so the validator's real integration with the new model's DB query is never run against a real blocked-email row.

The negative example in email_validator_spec.rb passes even if `validate_each` never calls `should_block?` at all — a Mocha `stubs` is not an expectation, and with no BlockedEmail rows in the test DB, 'validator skipped the check entirely' and 'check ran and returned false' are indistinguishable.
The EmailValidator spec never asserts which error message is produced (`user.email.blocked` vs `not_allowed`), so message regressions would go undetected.

The whitelist/blacklist domain-restriction branches relocated from `User#email_validator` into the new EmailValidator have no coverage — whitelist-set/not-matched, blacklist-set/matched, and blacklist-set/not-matched paths are never exercised because test settings are empty.

The `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard in EmailValidator is untested — a domain restriction error suppresses both the blocked-email check and its match_count/last_match_at side effects, and no test pins that interplay.

The regexp in `email_in_restriction_setting?` is unanchored, so `user@example.com.evil.org` matches a whitelist of `example.com` and `user@sub.example.com` bypasses a blacklist of `example.com` — security-relevant, admin-configured abuse-control edge cases that are untested.

No tests for the client-side `rejectedEmails` changes in create_account_controller.js — nothing verifies that a failed submit with `errors.email` pushes into `rejectedEmails`, that `emailValidation` then fails with `user.email.invalid`, or that the `.property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each')` dependency recomputes.

The client-side rejection trigger is over-broad: it pushes on any email error, including 'has already been taken' (uniqueness), after which the field shows the generic 'invalid' message for the rest of the session even though the actual problem was availability — and this behavioral contract is unpinned by any test on either the server JSON shape or the client consumption.

blocked_email_spec misses matching/normalization edge cases — `should_block?` uses an exact string match (`where(email: email)`) but every spec uses lowercase, correctly-formatted addresses, so behavior for case variants (e.g., `Block@SpamFromHome.ORG` vs stored lowercase) or whitespace is undefined; blocked rows seeded or imported with mixed case would silently never match.

Blocked-email stats update is performed via a DB write inside User validation (`should_block?` does `record.match_count += 1; record.save` from app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-16, reached from lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13), so the write joins the user save transaction and is silently rolled back with `ActiveRecord::Rollback` when the signup save fails — `match_count` and `last_match_at` never persist through the actual blocked-signup flow

Blocked-email lookup is an exact, case-sensitive string match with no normalization or downcasing (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:12), so blocking `bad@spam.com` is trivially bypassed by `Bad@Spam.com` or `BAD@spam.com`, defeating the anti-abuse purpose (the pre-existing domain checks were case-insensitive)

Increment of `match_count` is a non-atomic read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` with the return value ignored) in app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16, losing increments under concurrent signups and silently swallowing failed saves; should use an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")`

`action_type` column is declared `t.integer :action_type, null: false` with no database default in db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — the fallback exists only in the model's `before_validation` callback, so any insert bypassing callbacks (manual SQL loads, seeds, import scripts) fails with a NOT NULL violation

Client pushes any server-side email error into `rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js ~274-276) which is never cleared and renders the generic 'user.email.invalid' message (~69-74), so non-validity errors like uniqueness failures latch a misleading permanent 'invalid email' state that blocks retrying the same valid address for the session without a reload

BlockedEmail#should_block? queries the blocklist with an exact, case-sensitive, unnormalized `WHERE email = ?` (blocked_email.rb:11), and nothing in the signup path (User callbacks, controller, validator) downcases or strips the email, so an adversary can bypass the blocklist with variants like `EVIL@spam.com`, `evil@SPAM.com`, or a trailing space — which still deliver to the same mailbox and also evade the case-sensitive uniqueness check

create_account_controller.js pushes an email into `rejectedEmails` on any failed create with a truthy `result.errors.email`, conflating the new blocked-email check with unrelated errors like 'has already been taken' and 'is not allowed from that email provider'; once pushed, `emailValidation` permanently reports the generic `user.email.invalid` reason and `submitDisabled` blocks resubmission, misleading users whose valid email is merely taken

should_block? increments `match_count` via a non-atomic read-modify-write (load row, `match_count += 1`, save), so two concurrent signups with the same blocked email both read and save, silently losing one increment; it should use an atomic `update_all`/`increment_counter` style update instead
The return value of `record.save` inside should_block? is ignored, so a failed write silently loses the match statistic that serves as the admin-facing signal for whether to escalate blocking

should_block? performs a DB read and write (SELECT + UPDATE against a hot row) from inside User's validation pass, so a supposedly pure `valid?` now has side effects: the counter bumps even when the surrounding signup is aborted or rolls back, and it gives unauthenticated visitors a per-request write primitive that creates row-lock contention under the very signup flooding this feature exists to absorb

The EmailValidator spec instantiates the validator directly and stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` wholesale, so it would pass green even if User's `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` wiring were broken or the condition never fired on create, leaving the blocklist silently unenforced

No spec covers the contract between the controller's new `errors.email`/`values.email` payload shape and what `create_account_controller.js:274` consumes, so a key-name or serialization drift would leave the client guard silently dead while the server keeps rejecting

Instead it has two separate validations: `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` (no `if`) and `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`. Therefore presence/uniqueness are not conditionally disabled by `email_changed?`, and the described scenario (skipping all email validations on new records) is not supported by the change shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Increment of `match_count` is a non-atomic read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` with the return value ignored) in app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16, losing increments under concurrent signups and silently swallowing failed saves; should use an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")`

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?` the diff shows a read-modify-write increment (`record.match_count += 1` then `record.save`) and setting `last_match_at` before saving. This is non-atomic and can lose increments under concurrent calls, and the `save` result is ignored so a failed save would be silently swallowed. The suggested atomic update approach would avoid both issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `action_type` column is declared `t.integer :action_type, null: false` with no database default in db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5 — the fallback exists only in the model's `before_validation` callback, so any insert bypassing callbacks (manual SQL loads, seeds, import scripts) fails with a NOT NULL violation

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `blocked_emails.action_type` is `null: false` with no DB default (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb), while the only defaulting behavior is in the model callback `before_validation :set_defaults` (`self.action_type ||= BlockedEmail.actions[:block]`). So AR-created records will get a value, but any insert that bypasses validations/callbacks (raw SQL loads/import scripts) would hit a NOT NULL violation. That’s a diff-grounded robustness issue, though not a guaranteed runtime defect in the normal AR code path shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client pushes any server-side email error into `rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js ~274-276) which is never cleared and renders the generic 'user.email.invalid' message (~69-74), so non-validity errors like uniqueness failures latch a misleading permanent 'invalid email' state that blocks retrying the same valid address for the session without a reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` and, during `emailValidation`, immediately fails with generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` if `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` (create_account_controller.js ~65-79). On account creation failure, it pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present (~271-276). Nothing in the diff clears `rejectedEmails`, and the computed property depends on `rejectedEmails.@each`, so once an email triggers any server-side email error (e.g. uniqueness, domain not allowed, blocked), the client will permanently treat that email as “invalid” for the session and prevent retrying it, while also masking the specific server-side reason.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BlockedEmail#should_block? queries the blocklist with an exact, case-sensitive, unnormalized `WHERE email = ?` (blocked_email.rb:11), and nothing in the signup path (User callbacks, controller, validator) downcases or strips the email, so an adversary can bypass the blocklist with variants like `EVIL@spam.com`, `evil@SPAM.com`, or a trailing space — which still deliver to the same mailbox and also evade the case-sensitive uniqueness check

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) does an exact lookup via `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` (blocked_email.rb), and the new EmailValidator calls it with the raw `value` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb) without any downcasing/stripping. User email validation/uniqueness was changed to `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` and `validates :email, email: true` but likewise shows no normalization. As written, blocklist and uniqueness behavior will be case/whitespace sensitive at the app level, so variants like different case or trailing spaces can bypass BlockedEmail matching (and potentially uniqueness depending on DB collation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_account_controller.js pushes an email into `rejectedEmails` on any failed create with a truthy `result.errors.email`, conflating the new blocked-email check with unrelated errors like 'has already been taken' and 'is not allowed from that email provider'; once pushed, `emailValidation` permanently reports the generic `user.email.invalid` reason and `submitDisabled` blocks resubmission, misleading users whose valid email is merely taken

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, on any failed create where `result.errors.email` is truthy, the controller pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` (`pushObject(result.values.email)`). Then `emailValidation` immediately fails for any email contained in `rejectedEmails` and returns the generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, regardless of whether the underlying server-side email error was e.g. uniqueness (`has already been taken`), domain restriction (`user.email.not_allowed`), or the new blocked-email error (`user.email.blocked`). This conflates different email failures and forces subsequent validation for that same email to show a generic “invalid” reason (and likely disables submit if submit logic depends on `emailValidation`, though the exact `submitDisabled` implementation isn’t fully shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: should_block? increments `match_count` via a non-atomic read-modify-write (load row, `match_count += 1`, save), so two concurrent signups with the same blocked email both read and save, silently losing one increment; it should use an atomic `update_all`/`increment_counter` style update instead

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code does `record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` then mutates `record.match_count += 1` and `record.save` (also sets `last_match_at`). This is a classic non-atomic read/modify/write sequence; concurrent calls for the same `email` can overwrite each other and lose increments, leading to incorrect `match_count` (and potentially `last_match_at`). An atomic update (`update_all`, `increment_counter`, or `update_counters`) would avoid the lost-update issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The return value of `record.save` inside should_block? is ignored, so a failed write silently loses the match statistic that serves as the admin-facing signal for whether to escalate blocking

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code updates `match_count`/`last_match_at` and then calls `record.save` without checking the boolean return or raising on failure (`save!`). If the save were to fail (e.g., unexpected validation/db error), the method would still return the block decision (`record && record.action_type == ...`) but silently lose the statistics update. This is a real robustness/observability concern grounded in the diff, but not clearly a functional defect in the blocking decision itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: should_block? performs a DB read and write (SELECT + UPDATE against a hot row) from inside User's validation pass, so a supposedly pure `valid?` now has side effects: the counter bumps even when the surrounding signup is aborted or rolls back, and it gives unauthenticated visitors a per-request write primitive that creates row-lock contention under the very signup flooding this feature exists to absorb

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces side effects during validation: `User` now uses `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` (app/models/user.rb), and `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` when no prior email errors exist (lib/validators/email_validator.rb). `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a `where(...).first` and, if a record exists, increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and `save`s (app/models/blocked_email.rb). This means a `user.valid?`/failed `user.save` attempt can still write to `blocked_emails`, even though the user record is not created, and it provides unauthenticated requests a repeated write/lock point on the matching `blocked_emails` row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The EmailValidator spec instantiates the validator directly and stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` wholesale, so it would pass green even if User's `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` wiring were broken or the condition never fired on create, leaving the blocklist silently unenforced

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb the test calls `validator.validate_each(record, :email, record.email)` directly and stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so it only verifies EmailValidator’s internal behavior under stubbed conditions. It does not exercise the actual model-level wiring added in app/models/user.rb (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`), meaning the suite could still pass if the User validation hook were removed/misconfigured or the `if: :email_changed?` condition prevented the validator from running in real create/update flows. That’s a concrete test coverage gap introduced by this change, not a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers the contract between the controller's new `errors.email`/`values.email` payload shape and what `create_account_controller.js:274` consumes, so a key-name or serialization drift would leave the client guard silently dead while the server keeps rejecting

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new server failure payload shape in `UsersController#create` (`errors: user.errors.to_hash`, `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")`) and new client logic in `create_account_controller.js` that depends on that exact structure (`if (result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values) { ... pushObject(result.values.email); }`). The added specs cover `BlockedEmail` and `EmailValidator`, but nothing in the diff tests the controller JSON keys/serialization or that the client-side guard stays in sync with `errors.email` / `values.email`. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing integration/contract test rather than a proven runtime defect.
